ledger.note: 1700 BC: Arzawa appears in Western Anatolia with its capital at Apasa. Infobox 'Established: 1700 BC', capital 'Apaša'; the page dates no founding act, and its first dated event is Hattusili I's raid of c. 1650.

c. 1400 BC: Arzawa is subjugated by Tudhaliya I/II. 'they were subjugated by Tudhaliya I/II around 1400 BC, concurrently with the Assuwa Revolt'; the Assuwa page dates the 22-state western confederation to 'around 1400 BC'. The page says 'subjugated', not annexed or ruled by a governor, so it is drawn as vassalage; the Hittites dossier records the same year as a gain.

c. 1370 BC: Arzawa acts independently again (bridging judgment; the page gives no end to the subjugation). The next dated statement is that 'Around 1370 BC, during the reign of Tudhaliya III, Arzawa conquered a large portion of Western Anatolia', which presupposes freedom from Hatti.

ledger.note: c. 1320 BC: Mursili II and Uhha-Ziti fight for the Arzawa lands. Mursili II acceded in 1321 BC ('1321-1295 BC' short chronology) and 'turned to the West to resist the aggression of Uhhaziti, king of Arzawa'; the Arzawa page dates Uhha-Ziti to 1320-1300 BC and says 'When Mursili II ascended to the Hittite throne, much of Anatolia erupted into rebellion'; the Seha River Land page has the Hittites 'consolidated power over the region around 1320 BC, crushing a revolt in which the Seha River Land participated'. Neither page gives the campaign year.

notes: Cliopatria has no Arzawa; its Hittite shapes of -1400 (167,243 km2, east of 31.7 E) and -1300 (321,568 km2, west to 26.38 E) are the only drawn trace of Arzawa's land. No page opened gives a boundary or an area, so both keyframes are the researcher's reading of the lands the page lists and the reviewer should treat them as soft. The Hittites dossier (me-04-a) records the c. 1400 BC subjugation as a gain from arzawa and the c. 1300 BC settlement as a gain plus vassal_start for 'Mira-Kuwaliya, Hapalla and the Seha River Land'; this dossier agrees on the years but draws 1400-1370 as vassalage (the page says 'subjugated'). Pieces that the Hittites dossier names as vassals (Mira-Kuwaliya, Hapalla, the Seha River Land, later Wilusa) have no dossier; Mira has a page and was used only for its dates. Mursili II's Arzawa campaign year is not on any page opened (the page budget of five pages was spent; the Hittites page and Hattusili/Suppiluliuma pages were not opened).
